transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-03
Time: 11:00 AM PST
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Alex (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Jordan (Redwood SE), Maria (Brightwell CTO), Dan (Search Eng), Samir (Data Eng)

[00:00] Alex: Hey everyone thanks for joining, we'll keep this pretty demo-focused, show the Hosted API embeddings and rerank flow, and then go into Optimize suggestions. Maria, Dan, thanks for taking the time.
[00:12] Maria: Yep thanks, excited — our main pain is search relevance, lots of false positives, latency budget around 120ms for inline search.
[00:20] Alex: Understood, that's useful. Priya will drive the walkthrough and I'll jump in on product/packaging and next steps.
[00:28] Priya: Cool, quick agenda: 1) Hosted API embeddings endpoint, 2) how to do retrieval + rerank with Redwood's reranking endpoint, 3) Console + Optimize tips for batching/caching and quantization suggestions.
[00:39] Dan: Perfect. For context we currently use Elastic for candidate set and Pinecone for vectors — but Pinecone's cost at scale is getting high, and rerank is ad-hoc in our app.
[00:50] Priya: Great, so first demo: call the hosted embeddings endpoint, get vector for query, then do ANN lookup in your vector store, then call our rerank endpoint with the top-k candidates and the original query. We'll show an example payload.
[01:05] [00:60] Priya: (shares screen) Here's a code snippet — Node JS, but we also have Python examples. Request body: { model: "redwood-embed-1", input: query }. The response is an embedding array. Note: to minimize tokens and cost, use our compact embed model for search.
[01:24] Dan: Quick Q — what dimension sizes are we looking at? 1536? 1024?
[01:30] Priya: Good question. redwood-embed-1 is 1536 by default; we also have a 1024 quantized variant that trades quality for cost. Optimize can recommend the quantization profile by workload.
[01:42] Samir: How do you suggest we store embeddings — use our existing Pinecone or switch to dedicated Redwood index?
[01:48] Alex: Many customers keep their vector store and call Redwood for embeddings, then use Redwood rerank. We also partner with vector stores — but you can keep Pinecone if you like, or use a lightweight Redis/FAISS setup.
[01:59] Priya: Next, rerank endpoint: you send { model: "redwood-rerank-1", query: q, candidates: [ {id, content, embedding?} ] } and we return a scored list. The big win is the rerank model considers query-document interaction, which recovers recall from the ANN.
[02:18] [02:15] Priya: (demo runs) Example payload with 10 candidates, end-to-end time from request to rerank response here is ~85ms in our test environment. That's hosted latency — your mileage depends on region and qps.
[02:33] Dan: 85ms is promising. Our 120ms budget includes Elastic query time — so we need the whole pipeline under that.
[02:41] Priya: Right, caching and prefix/KV cache can help — if you have repeat queries we can serve from cache for sub-10ms. Also batching multiple rerank operations helps throughput but adds latency; Optimize suggests batch sizes by your qps/latency SLO.
[02:56] Maria: For security, we need SOC 2, SSO, SAML, and audit logs. Also data retention rules — logs can't keep PII beyond 30 days.
[03:07] Alex: We have SOC 2 and will send the security packet. Hosted API has configurable audit logs and retention; we do offer options for shorter retention and can exclude storing raw inputs if needed. We also support SAML/SSO and RBAC.
[03:20] Samir: Any data inferences left on Redwood? Are embeddings considered PII?
[03:25] Priya: Embeddings are derived and we treat them as customer data; you can opt out of retention and we can rotate keys. For strict regimes, our Private deployment is available.
[03:33] Dan: On cost — what's the per-embedding and per-rerank cost ballpark?
[03:38] Alex: I'll send exact pricing but ballpark: the compact embed model is cheaper per unit; rerank is charged per candidate processed. We'll include a calculator in the pricing doc so you can model cost at your qps.
[03:50] [04:00] Priya: Now quick Console tour — Dashboard shows per-route latency, token counts, and rerank-specific metrics. Optimize gives suggestions: recommended batch size, cache TTL, and a quantization recommendation.
[04:12] Priya: (navigates) Here's the Optimize tab — it flagged that for search workloads with sub-200ms SLOs we recommend small batch sizes (1-4) and prefix caching for top queries. It also suggested testing a 4-bit quantized model for the candidate generation path.
[04:28] Dan: If we switch to a quantized model for embed generation, how big is the quality degradation?
[04:33] Priya: Usually small for nearest-neighbor recall — Optimize can run a quick A/B on your labeled set to show expected delta. We'll run a regression check during the pilot.
[04:43] Maria: Can you show a rerank example where Elastic returns a bunch of lexical matches but rerank surfaces the semantically relevant doc?
[04:50] Priya: Sure, give me a sample query.
[04:54] Dan: "How to reverse a transaction in our payments system" — Elastic returns policy pages first but they're not exactly the how-to.
[05:00] [05:00] Priya: (runs demo) Right here the rerank rescored a deeper KB article that has the exact steps; score moved it from position 8 to 1. You can see the score deltas in the response.
[05:12] Samir: Nice; I see. That would reduce manual support tickets.
[05:17] Alex: Quick note on reliability — Hosted API has regional routing and automatic fallback to compatible model variants if a zone is constrained. For strict enterprise SLAs you'd consider Dedicated.
[05:29] Maria: Timeline-wise we want to pilot in April and potentially go to Dedicated by Q3 if results are positive. Is that feasible?
[05:36] Alex: Absolutely, pilot in April makes sense. We'll scope a 4-week pilot with success criteria (NDCG improvement, latency under 120ms at target qps).
[05:44] [05:45] Dan: About quota and rate limits — how are those handled for hosted API?
[05:48] Alex: We give baseline quotas; for pilots we can raise limits. There are rate limit headers in responses so you can monitor. For consistent high throughput, Dedicated provides reserved GPU pools.
[05:58] Maria: Any compliance concerns if we send customer emails or PII in the query?
[06:02] Priya: You can configure redaction on the client side or use on-the-fly redact in the ingest pipeline; we advise not to send raw PII. We can also set retention to zero for such data.
[06:12] Jordan: I'll follow up with a short how-to doc: best practices for redaction + prefix caching integration.
[06:18] Samir: Great. A quick micro-question — can the rerank call accept precomputed embeddings to avoid recomputing on our side?
[06:24] Priya: Yes, you can include candidate embeddings in the rerank payload which speeds things and reduces tokens.
[06:30] Dan: Any SDKs for rerank?
[06:32] Priya: We have JS and Python SDKs with helpers for constructing rerank payloads and streaming results.
[06:38] [06:40] Alex: Ok let's recap next steps and open items. Priya will share example payloads and a benchmark harness; Jordan will provide caching how-to; Alex will send pricing and security docs. Maria will share dataset and expected qps.
[06:52] Maria: Sounds good — one ask, can you include a sample SLA for latency?
[06:56] Alex: Yes we'll include typical SLOs for Hosted and options for Dedicated SLAs in the packet.
[07:02] Dan: On the pilot metrics — we want a baseline run from our current pipeline (Elastic + Pinecone) so we can compare NDCG and latency.
[07:09] Priya: We'll help instrument that baseline and run the Redwood-hosted rerank on the same candidate sets.
[07:15] Samir: Anything else on integrations? We use GCP; any region constraints?
[07:19] Alex: We have hosted regions in US/Europe and more coming; for strict data residency we can discuss Private.
[07:25] [07:30] Maria: Thanks all — good session. We'll expect the packet and trial planning invite.
[07:33] Alex: Thanks everyone, will follow up.

Transcript notes: Occasional mis-transcriptions present (e.g., K V cash instead of KV cache), some speaker attribution simplified. Occasional filler words and interruptions preserved.
